fields.statement: QA at a7cdc22a, hands-on with the built binary against a build of parent c403ceb0. On a clone of the real rhiza repo (1305 change sets, 31 not landed), for every non-landed change set plus a missing ID, ran tree (capability and intent, --retired), ls --retired over all pages, slice --change and show with --view what-if:<cs> under both binaries: byte-identical output (withdrawn ones give the same conflict error, the missing one the same not_found). The whole sweep took 108 s with the parent and 16 s with this build. Running the new binary over an index the parent built (schema upgrade) gave identical output too, as did the change set 01M6BH7Z itself on a clone of the branch head. In a fresh scratch repo, wrote step by step with the new binary (an intention adding a child, setting a landed node and retiring a decision; a second one linking and depending on it; a third with a stale-base conflict once the first landed; a fourth depending on the unlanded third and editing its new node, plus retires) and after each of 9 steps compared every in-flight what-if read against the parent on a fresh copy: identical each time, with the incremental index catch-up in between. Spot-checked: c-node reads cn under what-if:C and cn2 under the dependent D.
